Cyber Attack Disrupts New Zealand Telco Firms, Services Impacted Nationwide

A significant cyber attack targeting multiple telecommunications firms in New Zealand has caused widespread disruption across the industry, leaving thousands of customers facing outages and degraded services. The incident, which began late Tuesday evening, involves a ransomware variant believed to have infiltrated the core IT infrastructure of several major telcos, including Southern Signal and KiwiNet Communications.

According to statements released by affected companies, the attack has crippled customer-facing portals, billing systems, and, in some cases, network management tools. “We are experiencing a major technical incident impacting both our mobile and broadband platforms,” said Amanda Kerr, Chief Operating Officer of Southern Signal, in a press briefing Wednesday morning. “Our teams are working around the clock with cybersecurity experts and government agencies to contain the breach and restore services.”

The Telecommunications Association of New Zealand (TANZ) has issued an industry-wide alert, urging all providers to heighten their cyber defenses. “This attack highlights the growing sophistication of threat actors targeting our sector,” said TANZ Chairperson Hari Patel. “It’s critical for all operators to review their security protocols and ensure robust incident response plans are in place.”

Initial analysis suggests the attackers gained access via compromised remote access credentials. While no customer financial data has been confirmed stolen, service disruptions have affected an estimated 500,000 users across Auckland, Wellington, and Christchurch. Customers have reported difficulties making calls, sending messages, and accessing online accounts.

Frontline staff at KiwiNet Communications described a surge in call centre volumes as customers sought updates. “We’re asking for patience as we work to resolve this unprecedented issue,” said union spokesperson Maia Rangi. “Our priority is supporting affected customers and protecting their information.”

Industry analysts warn that the economic impact could escalate if the situation persists. “Telecommunications are the backbone of New Zealand’s digital economy,” noted Liam Foster of Pacific Tech Insights. “Extended downtime could have a ripple effect on businesses and consumers, underlining the critical need for resilient infrastructure.”

Both Southern Signal and KiwiNet Communications have declined to comment on whether a ransom demand has been received. The National Cyber Security Centre continues to investigate the source and scope of the breach.

At the time of writing, restoration timelines remain unclear, with service providers pledging regular updates as recovery efforts continue.
